verdicts.message: AnalyzerSeverityNone: CA2007 — this rule is switched off for every file the section matches, in every project under this directory, and the only record that it was ever switched off is this line: nothing at the sites it would have reported says so, so a reader of that code has no reason to look here, and code added years from now inherits the decision silently. Fix what the rule reports and delete the entry, or — where some sites really are legitimate — leave the rule on and suppress it at those sites with their reasons, so it keeps protecting the rest of the tree. If the rule is genuinely unwanted here, say why — on this line after the entry, or in the comment run directly above it: a comment that only repeats the rule's own title is read as no explanation at all and leaves this row in place.

verdicts.message: High: watchdog-secret-interpolated-into-run: A secret is interpolated straight into this `run:` script. Actions expands `${{ }}` BEFORE the shell exists, so the literal secret value is what gets written into the step's script file on the runner's disk and passed to the shell as code — not as data. Quoting does not change that. From there it reaches every place the script itself reaches: the on-disk script, any shell trace (`set -x`, `bash -v`), a `ps` listing of the commands it launches, and any error text that echoes the failing command. Log masking does not cover those, and a secret cannot be un-leaked once it is on a runner you do not own. Bind the secret to an `env:` entry on the step instead (`env:` `MY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MY_TOKEN }}`) and reference that ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE from the script using your shell's own syntax (`"$MY_TOKEN"` in bash, `$env:MY_TOKEN` in PowerShell), so the value is passed to the process as data and is never substituted into the script text.
verdicts.reason: True and it is plant IAC-018 (the deploy token interpolated into the run script and onto kubectl's command line). The harness maps this rule to ci-secret-exposure while the key labels the plant secret-in-process-arguments, so it scores as unmatched.
verdicts.action: none in the repo (it is the plant); coordinator: map watchdog-secret-interpolated-into-run to secret-in-process-arguments or declare a family

verdicts.message: High IaC: DS-0002: Image user should not be 'root'. Specify at least 1 USER command in Dockerfile with non-root user as argument. Add 'USER <non root user name>' line to the Dockerfile. A container that starts as root runs your process with root's capabilities inside the namespace, so a compromise of the process starts from there. The step: create an unprivileged account in the image (`RUN useradd -r -M app` — or whatever this base image's account tooling is, `adduser` and `useradd` are not both present everywhere`), give it ownership of the paths the process writes at runtime (`COPY --chown=` on those layers, or a `RUN chown -R`), and end the final stage with `USER app` so it is the default at start. Build stages that only compile can stay root; it is the stage that RUNS that needs the account. If the process genuinely requires root — it manages the container runtime, ptraces another process or opens raw devices — say so here rather than making a change that breaks it.
verdicts.reason: DS-0002 is plant IAC-001 (no USER), reported at line 1. The absence holds for the whole file, so the key's stage-range site was too narrow.
verdicts.action: key fixed: IAC-001 is a whole-file entry

verdicts.message: Unpinned build actions: CI references GitHub Actions by a floating ref (@main / @tag) rather than a pinned commit SHA, weakening build integrity. 1 floating ref(s) across 1 workflow file(s). Each floating ref is itemized at file:line by the SAST (D29) lens. `.github/dependabot.yml` declares an updater for the `github-actions` ecosystem, so pinning does not freeze these steps: the updater rewrites SHA pins as new releases ship, which makes this posture near-zero maintenance to hold once taken.

verdicts.message: Secret passed as a command-line argument: 2 CI command(s) pass a credential in the command line (as an argument of its own, or attached to an option as `--flag=<secret>`), where it is visible in the runner's process table to any other process on the host (and to anything that logs a command line): .github/workflows/deploy.yml: kubectl --server "$KUBE_SERVER" --token "${{ secrets.KUBE_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}" apply --recursive -f deploy/k8s; .github/workflows/deploy.yml: kubectl --server "$KUBE_SERVER" --token "${{ secrets.KUBE_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}" -n depot-slots rollout status deployment/depot-slots-api --timeout=5m. Pass the credential through the environment instead (an `env:` mapping on the step, read by the tool from its own variable) or on stdin, so it never appears in an argument vector.

verdicts.message: Workflow token grant is wider than its jobs use: 1 `permissions:` grant(s) are wider than the jobs that hold them use (release.yml:7 (write-all; held by images)). `write-all` grants every scope GitHub defines — contents, packages, actions, id-token, security-events, pages, deployments and the rest — and no job needs all of them; a named write scope declared at the top of a workflow is inherited by every job that declares no block of its own, including the ones that only build. GitHub Actions has no step-level `permissions:`, so wherever the grant is held it is live for every step of that job: the build and dependency-install steps run build scripts, install hooks and plugins from the whole transitive dependency tree, and any one of them can read the token and commit to the repository, publish its packages or attest its artifacts. Declare `permissions: {contents: read}` at the top of the workflow, and name the exact write scopes — and only those — on the one job that publishes.
verdicts.reason: Is plant IAC-015 ('release.yml:7 (write-all ...)' in the message) but carries no SARIF location.
verdicts.action: none (plant); location-less false negative of IAC-015

verdicts.message: No DR/backup evidence: A persistence guard (data volume / purge-protection) was found, but no backup, geo-recovery or RTO/RPO controls were evidenced — a volume that survives a container recreate is not a tested restore from catastrophic loss.
verdicts.reason: Accurate: no backup/RTO evidence - the deliberate posture of BND-005.

falseNegatives.reason: hostNetwork: true (daemonset.yaml:20) is reported by KSV-0009 on the DaemonSet's spec (line 9) and by CKV_K8S_19 at line 1, both outside the ±3 tolerance; the plant is on the exact line. Location imprecision, not a missing rule.

The read-write containerd-socket hostPath (daemonset.yaml:71-74) is reported only by KSV-0023 at line 9 (the DaemonSet spec), one row for all hostPath volumes; it never names the socket. Location imprecision.
Ingress without a tls: section serving the bearer-token API over plain HTTP: no rule fires (no trivy/checkov/semgrep check for Ingress TLS in the pinned rule sets).
permissions: write-all (release.yml:7) is reported by D36 'Workflow token grant is wider than its jobs use' with the site in the message but no SARIF location, so it cannot match a located entry.
falseNegatives.note: From the harness-1.3 re-score on, the D36 row is matched through the location named in its message (locationSource: message); TP in every scan scored since, including v1.2-iter1.

falseNegatives.reason: pull_request_target that checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha and docker-builds it with the registry token in env: neither pull-request-target-code-checkout nor any custom rule fired.
falseNegatives.withdrawnReason: Plant defect, corrected in v1.2.0: line 34 of .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml was invalid YAML (an unquoted plain scalar containing ': '), so neither GitHub, actionlint nor the scanner's semgrep could parse the file and the plant was invisible to every parser. The iteration-2 FN verdict was a judging error. With the line quoted (shell text unchanged), pull-request-target-code-checkout fires at line 16 and IAC-017 scores TP (scan v1.2-iter1).

falseNegatives.reason: kubectl --token "${{ secrets.KUBE_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}" (deploy.yml:33-34): D36 'Secret passed as a command-line argument' reports it without a SARIF location; semgrep watchdog-secret-interpolated-into-run reports it at line 32 but the mapping assigns that rule to ci-secret-exposure.
falseNegatives.note: From the harness-1.3 re-score on, semgrep watchdog-secret-interpolated-into-run at deploy.yml:32 matches through the corrected secret-in-process-arguments mapping (within line tolerance of 33-34); TP in every scan scored since, including v1.2-iter1.

falseNegatives.reason: Missing liveness/readiness probes on the reminder worker container (deployment.yaml:24-41): checkov CKV_K8S_8/CKV_K8S_9 report it, but at line 1 of the document, outside the tolerance. Under the coarse v1.0.0 concept it was scored TP via an unrelated registry-allow-list row on the container line; with the precise concept (key v1.1.0+) it is an FN by location. Found at file level.

scoreBands.note: D41 credits seccomp found anywhere in the YAML blob (one of three workloads sets RuntimeDefault) as if every workload had it; AppArmor/SELinux absent. Band set before the first scan and kept.
D42 is gated on cluster-governance resources the repository does not ship, so the absence of runtime detection/admission is not scored. Leniency; band kept.
LA4 made no model call in the host --with-llm pass (absent from llm-calls.json and the scorecard).

observations: D31's checkov pass reports Kubernetes findings at line 1 of the document (and trivy pod-level checks on the workload's spec), so container- and pod-level defects are often located far from their site: two plants are FNs purely by location, and ~40 line-1 rows restate found plants (redundant).

D36 reports workflow-level findings (write-all, secret on the command line, unpinned actions) without a SARIF location even when the message names file:line; located plants cannot be matched (same harness gap as bench-csharp-security-dependencies).

IAC-010 (missing probes) is scored TP via KSV-0125 (registry allow-list) on the container line, because both map to iac-misconfiguration; the real probe rows (CKV_K8S_8/9) are at line 1. The concept is too coarse to tell them apart.

Harness decision for the coordinator: watchdog-secret-interpolated-into-run is mapped to ci-secret-exposure; the taxonomy describes that concept as secrets reaching untrusted code. A secret expanded into a run script is closer to secret-in-process-arguments (CWE-214) - remap or declare a family.
No rule for Ingress TLS and no firing for pull_request_target + head checkout + build: both are clean misses on high-impact plants.

All 20 traps that probe a located site were left alone (digest pins with 'latest' in a comment, numeric USER, emptyDir, anchor/merge-key probes, ExternalSecret, SealedSecret ciphertext, pull_request_target without checkout, env-passed secrets, SHA-pinned first-party actions). The two caught traps are both 'no HEALTHCHECK' on Kubernetes-only images.
Engine bug already noted by the coordinator still applies: WD-K8S-0004 is the automount rule here (IAC-011).

v1.1.0 / harness 1.3: IAC-010 missing probes is a true FN (probe rows are reported at line 1); IAC-015 and IAC-018 are found via message-named locations / the corrected secret-in-process-arguments mapping.

v1.2.0 correction: the earlier observation that nothing fired for pull_request_target + head checkout + build was wrong about the scanner. The plant's workflow file was invalid YAML (pr-preview.yml:34) and no parser could read it; once valid, pull-request-target-code-checkout reports it at line 16. Remaining FNs at v1.2.0: IAC-004, IAC-006, IAC-010 (all Kubernetes rows located at line 1 / the spec rather than the site) and IAC-013 (no Ingress-TLS rule).
